expert_diagnosis: Luckin Coffee's reported growth was substantially fabricated through inflated transaction volumes. The business model's reliance on aggressive discounting and app-based ordering was used to conceal weak unit economics and to generate false revenue figures. Internal controls were deliberately or negligently inadequate to prevent systematic financial-statement manipulation. The governance and audit framework failed to detect or prevent fabrication at scale.
expert_first_action: Independent verification of transaction authenticity through forensic audit of all app-based sales data, cash conversion at store level, and expense records before any further capital allocation or expansion decisions.
actual_decision: Luckin Coffee disclosed on 2 April 2020 that an internal investigation had identified fabricated transactions totaling approximately RMB 2.2 billion. SEC subsequently alleged fabricated retail sales exceeding $300 million and inflated expenses of over $190 million.
harmful_actions: Fabrication of transaction volumes to inflate reported revenue
Use of aggressive discount promotions to generate artificial transaction activity
Failure to maintain adequate internal controls to prevent or detect financial-statement manipulation
Governance and audit committee failure to independently verify revenue quality
Capital raised from investors based on materially false growth metrics
beneficial_actions: Internal investigation that led to the 2 April 2020 disclosure
SEC enforcement action provided accountability and investor protection mechanism
Company eventually restructured and re-emerged under new management with stronger controls
citation: SEC Litigation Release LR-24987 on Luckin Coffee accounting fraud settlement. Wharton case study on Luckin Coffee. Academic analysis of Luckin fraud mechanics.
actual_outcome: 2 April 2020: Luckin disclosed fabricated transactions of approximately RMB 2.2 billion. SEC alleged fabricated retail sales over $300 million and inflated expenses over $190 million. Luckin agreed to pay $180 million to settle SEC accounting fraud charges. Company delisted from Nasdaq. Eventually restructured and relisted on OTC markets under new management.
documented_root_causes: Revenue-quality failure through fabricated transaction volumes
Accounting fraud in reported sales and expense records
False growth signal used to raise capital and build market position
Weak internal controls deliberately or negligently inadequate
Discount-driven unit economics concealing unviable store-level profitability
Governance and audit failure to independently verify financial statements
Investor-confidence built on materially false reported growth
final_business_state: Disclosed RMB 2.2 billion in fabricated transactions. Delisted from Nasdaq. Paid $180 million SEC settlement. Restructured under new management. Eventually relisted on OTC markets with reformed governance.
